assessments.reasoning: The six verified ranges in Mozilla’s English instrument identify the covered material, distinguish its forms, supply the incorporated source-distribution terms, and state the executable trigger and access conditions. The conjunction in section 3.2(a) defeats the archive-only reading.

challenge.method: Tested a working source archive whose location is never communicated, a prompt offer priced above distribution cost, and an offer at cost fulfilled only after an unreasonable delay.
challenge.results: Each fails a distinct part of section 3.2(a). Source availability alone leaves the information duty unmet. Prompt delivery cannot cure excessive charges, and charging at cost cannot cure untimely access. A high absolute cost also calls for examining whether the means are reasonable.

limitations: The source duty concerns Covered Software. The text supplies neither a fixed deadline nor a monetary ceiling independent of distribution cost. Section 4 qualifies the duty in cases of legal impossibility.
reasoning: Section 3.2(a) imposes two duties on distribution of covered executable material. The distributor must make the covered source available on the section 3.1 terms and tell executable recipients how to obtain it. The means must be reasonable, delivery timely, and the charge at most the cost of distribution to the recipient.
